To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Tennessee Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Askew is seeking documentation establishing what medical evaluation and treatment Carruthers received after botched execution , whether an ambulance was requested, and whether hospital transportation was considered.

The request calls on the Tennessee Department of Correction and Governor Bill Lee’s administration to:

I * Release emergency-response timelines for both incidents.
* Explain when medical personnel evaluated each person and what treatment was provided, consistent with patient privacy and authorization.
* Identify who decided whether ambulance transportation or hospital care was necessary.
* Explain any differences in the responses based on documented injuries and medical needs.
* Include Carruthers’ treatment and emergency preparedness in the independent review ordered after Pike’s failed execution.

The circumstances differed: Pike received execution drugs, while Carruthers’ attempt was halted during efforts to establish intravenous access. Those differences make medical documentation essential to assessing whether each received appropriate care. (apnews.com, washingtonpost.com)

Askew’s call seeks answers rather than assuming that the available public reporting establishes unequal treatment. Tennessee should provide a clear account of its decisions and the safeguards available when an execution attempt causes injury or a medical emergency.

Every person in state custody deserves timely, appropriate medical care. Transparency is necessary to determine what happened, whether that standard was met, and what must change.

Media Contact:
Donald Askew Jr.
Follow the Shaw Files Campaign

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Kent Hoover, a citizen of Tennessee, in coordination with Donald R. Askew Jr..
